slides.title: SQL vs NoSQL
slides.html:
Databases

SQL vs NoSQL

SQL (relational)

Tables with fixed columns, joined by keys. Strict structure.

PostgreSQL, MySQL

NoSQL (document)

Flexible JSON-like documents. Fast to start with.

MongoDB

Both are good

Pick by the data, not hype. You'll meet both in jobs.

learn the ideas

slides.title: MongoDB concepts
slides.html:
MongoDB

MongoDB concepts

  • Database → one per app
  • Collection → group of documents
  • Document → one record (BSON)
  • Every document has a unique _id

A document

// collection: tasks
{
  "_id": ObjectId("6750a1f2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0"),
  "title": "Learn MongoDB",
  "done": false,
  "tags": ["backend", "week4"],
  "createdAt": ISODate("2026-11-21T10:00:00Z")
}

slides.title: Environment variables
slides.html:
Secrets

Environment variables

  • Secrets go in .env
  • .env goes in .gitignore
  • Commit .env.example with empty values
  • Node 20+: node --env-file=.env

.env

# .env
PORT=5000
MONGO_URI=mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster0.../taskdb
 
# .gitignore
node_modules
.env
 
# package.json
"dev": "node --watch --env-file=.env server.js"

slides.title: Connecting with Mongoose
slides.html:
Connect

Connecting with Mongoose

  • Connect once when the app starts
  • Start listening only after it connects
  • Exit if it fails

server.js

import mongoose from "mongoose";
 
try {
  await mongoose.connect(process.env.MONGO_URI);
  console.log("✅ MongoDB connected");
  app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`API on ${PORT}`));
} catch (err) {
  console.error("❌ MongoDB connection failed:", err.message);
  process.exit(1);
}

slides.title: Schemas and models
slides.html:
Schema

Schemas and models

  • A schema sets the shape and rules
  • A model queries the collection
  • timestamps adds createdAt/updatedAt

models/Task.js

import mongoose from "mongoose";
 
const taskSchema = new mongoose.Schema(
  {
    title: { type: String, required: true, trim: true, maxlength: 200 },
    done: { type: Boolean, default: false },
    priority: { type: String, enum: ["low", "medium", "high"],
                default: "medium" },
    dueDate: Date,
  },
  { timestamps: true }
);
 
export default mongoose.model("Task", taskSchema);

slides.title: CRUD with Mongoose
slides.html:
CRUD

CRUD with Mongoose

  • Every call returns a Promise
  • find returns an array
  • findById returns null if missing

controllers/tasks.js

await Task.create({ title: "Learn Mongoose" });
await Task.find({ done: false }).sort({ createdAt: -1 });
await Task.findById(id);
await Task.findByIdAndUpdate(id, { done: true },
  { new: true, runValidators: true });
await Task.findByIdAndDelete(id);
await Task.countDocuments({ done: true });

slides.title: Query operators
slides.html:
Filters

Query operators

  • Operators start with $
  • Combine conditions in one object
  • $regex for simple search

Querying

Task.find({ priority: { $in: ["high", "medium"] } });
Task.find({ dueDate: { $lt: new Date() }, done: false }); // overdue
Task.find({ title: { $regex: "mongo", $options: "i" } });
Task.find({ $or: [{ done: true }, { priority: "low" }] });
 
Task.find().select("title done").limit(10).skip(20);

slides.title: Common Mongoose errors
slides.html:
Errors

Common Mongoose errors

ValidationError

A required field is missing or a rule failed.

→ 400

CastError

"abc" isn't a valid ObjectId.

→ 400 or 404

Duplicate key

A unique field already exists (code 11000).

→ 409

slides.title: The controller, now async
slides.html:
Build

The controller, now async

  • Same routes, same responses
  • await every database call
  • Express 5 forwards thrown errors

controllers/tasks.js

import Task from "../models/Task.js";
 
export const list = async (req, res) => {
  const filter = {};
  if (req.query.done) filter.done = req.query.done === "true";
  if (req.query.q) filter.title = { $regex: req.query.q, $options: "i" };
  res.json(await Task.find(filter).sort({ createdAt: -1 }));
};
 
export const create = async (req, res) => {
  const { title, priority, dueDate } = req.body;
  res.status(201).json(await Task.create({ title, priority, dueDate }));
};
